title: Operate and Troubleshoot Search
readerIntent: Qualify, monitor, recover, and tune a configured search provider.
priorKnowledge: Know the selected engine, topology, tenant routing, mappings, and consistency policy.
owner: Configured search provider and deployment operators
summary: Production search requires live-provider security, health, capacity, recovery, mapping, and consistency qualification beyond deterministic framework tests.

sections.heading: Monitor
items: Connection and cluster health.
Query, indexing, and bulk latency.
Rejected operations and partial failures.
Indexing lag and reconciliation results.
Mapping conflicts and alias migration.
Index size, shard/replica capacity, and cache effects.
Safe tenant-aware error and throughput dimensions.

sections.heading: Secure
items: Use TLS, authenticated engine access, restricted credentials, and secret governance.
Keep management endpoints and provider diagnostics out of public routes.
Preserve tenant routing and authorization before query execution.
Do not log unrestricted query content, credentials, or raw provider errors.

sections.heading: Recover
items: Define reconnect and bounded retry behavior.
Reconcile the derived index from authoritative records.
Use versioned indexes and aliases for incompatible mapping migrations.
Qualify snapshot/restore according to the engine and deployment.
Test degraded startup, provider outage, reconnect, reindex, rollback, and cleanup.

sections.heading: Local versus production
paragraphs: A locally running Elasticsearch instance proves integration mechanics only. Production qualification must cover authentication, encryption, supported versions, capacity, high availability, backup, recovery, monitoring, and incident procedures.

sections.heading: Capacity and performance
items: Measure representative text, filter, sort, aggregation, and pagination queries.
Bound result windows, query complexity, bulk size, and concurrency.
Size shards, replicas, storage, memory, and headroom from measured workload.
Observe indexing pressure, merges, refresh cost, and query cache.
Run load and soak tests with tenant routing and expected growth.

sections.heading: Incident examples
items: Red cluster: protect writes and queries according to policy, restore allocation, and verify consistency.
Indexing lag: identify authority throughput, queue, rejects, provider pressure, and retry state.
Mapping conflict: stop incompatible documents, version the mapping, reindex, and cut over safely.
Wrong-tenant result: disable affected search, preserve evidence, repair routing, and assess exposure.
Slow query: capture safe shape, inspect plan, bound behavior, and regression-test changes.

sections.heading: Backup and recovery
paragraphs: Because search is derived, rebuilding from authoritative data is the primary correctness path. Engine snapshots can reduce recovery time but do not replace reconciliation.
Test snapshot restore, full reindex, alias recovery, permission checks, and recovery objectives with production-representative volume.

sections.heading: Readiness evidence
items: Supported-version and provider maturity record.
Security and tenant-isolation review.
Load, soak, outage, node-loss, and recovery tests.
Reindex, alias rollback, and snapshot restore.
Dashboards, alerts, runbooks, on-call ownership, and capacity headroom.
Current limitations and requalification schedule.
